subject: Air-gapped deployment readiness — follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@heliosbio.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment follow-up & next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a short list of clarifying items so we can put together an on-site readiness plan and SOW draft.

Recap (what we heard)
- Target: private, air-gapped deployment inside Helios Bio datacenter for inference of clinical NLP models.
- Constraint: no general internet egress from compute nodes; jump host allowed for signed packages.
- Initial scale: pilot cluster (targeting 6-8 GPUs) with future ramp to ~32 GPUs.
- SLA/ops: Helios will own hardware; Redwood provides inference runtime + ops playbook.

Clarifying questions (we'll use these to prepare an offline bundle and runbook):
1) Hardware inventory: can you confirm exact GPU model(s), CPU, RAM, and NVMe capacity per node?
2) OS and image management: current OS version and whether you permit kernel-level updates applied from offline media?
3) Upgrade window: preferred maintenance windows and blackout periods (monthly/quarterly)?
4) Network: is there a restricted jump host we can use for secure package transfer? Are outbound connections to specific Redwood IPs allowed through the jump?
5) Backups: where do you want stateful data (KV cache snapshots, audit logs) stored — on-site SAN or encrypted removable media?
6) Security/compliance: any additional attestations needed (SOC2/HIPAA language we should include in SOW)?

Attachments: I attached our initial onprem checklist and an anonymized network diagram to help you map items to the questions above.

Next steps
- If you can share the inventory PDF (or confirm answers above) we'll assemble a signed offline package (tarball) and a runbook draft for your SREs.
- Proposed times for an on-site readiness/ops deep-dive with our SRE lead: Tue 21 Sep 09:00-11:00 PT or Wed 22 Sep 13:00-15:00 PT.

Thanks — I can take the first pass on the SOW language once we lock the inventory.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[t] +1 415-555-0123
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@heliosbio.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Sarah Kim <s.kim@heliosbio.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment follow-up & next steps

Tessa — thanks for the concise summary. Answers inline below.

1) Hardware inventory:
- Nodes (pilot): 3 x rack servers, each with 2x NVIDIA A100 40GB, dual-socket AMD EPYC, 512GB RAM, 4x 2TB NVMe.
- Long-term plan: we expect to expand by adding identical racks; procurement timeline in Q1 2027.

2) OS/image management:
- Current: Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, minimal footprint. Kernel/OS patches are allowed but must be applied via approved offline media; no direct apt-get from internet.

3) Upgrade window:
- Preferred maintenance window: Saturdays 02:00–06:00 local (PT). Monthly cadence acceptable.

4) Network:
- We have a hardened jump host in a DMZ that can be used to transfer signed packages via SFTP. Outbound connections from the jump host can be whitelisted to specific Redwood IPs (we will provide the jump host's egress restrictions doc).

5) Backups:
- KV cache snapshots should be stored on our on-prem SAN (Encrypted at rest). Long-term export for compliance can be delivered on encrypted removable media.

6) Security/compliance:
- HIPAA controls apply for any PHI-containing payloads; we'll need SOC2-related artifacts and a short description of logging/audit surfaces in the SOW.

I attached our internal inventory PDF for the pilot nodes and a short requirements note.

We can do the readiness call on Tue 21 Sep 09:00 PT. Please put my SRE (Sarah Kim) and our infra lead on the invite.

—Alex
Alex Turner
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Helios Bio
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@heliosbio.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment follow-up & next steps

Alex — appreciate the quick answers and the inventory PDF. A few technical notes and concrete recommendations from our side to make the on-site readiness call productive: 

High-level approach
- Offline bundle: Redwood will produce a signed, checksummed tarball that contains the runtime binaries, dependency wheelhouse, and a small upgrade agent. The bundle will be delivered to your jump host for SFTP pull.
- Staging: we strongly recommend a staging VLAN or one pilot node configured as a mirror for upgrades to validate the bundle prior to cluster-wide rollout.

Minimum recommended pilot config (for realistic perf testing)
- 8 GPUs total (we can run a pilot with your 3 nodes but performance staging is limited at 6 GPUs).
- NVMe per-node for KV cache and local model shards (we recommend at least 2TB NVMe per GPU).
- Dedicated management interface for orchestration traffic.

Upgrade and offline ops
- Upgrade plan: scheduled monthly; Redwood provides pre-check scripts that run on the jump host (permissions-limited) and an upgrade sequence: (1) push to staging node, (2) smoke test, (3) staggered rollout across compute nodes.
- Signed USB fallback: we will also provide a USB-signed fallback image if network transfer via jump host is disrupted.
- Rollback: we keep snapshot/metadata to rollback within the same window for the first 72 hours after an upgrade.

Deliverables ahead of the call
- Draft on-prem SOW and runbook (we'll populate with your inventory fields).
- Offline package build instructions and sample checklist (confluence link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RD/airgapped-runbook).

Question for Helios procurement
- Do you prefer Redwood to handle the orchestration/control plane (we run a small private control plane appliance in your DMZ) or do you want 100% customer-managed control plane? Both are supported but have different support SLAs and pricing.

I'll prepare a short technical slide (30 min) for the readiness call covering the upgrade flow and rollback. Tessa — please confirm the invite with Alex and Sarah for Tue 21 Sep 09:00 PT.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@heliosbio.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:02:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment follow-up & next steps

Sounds good — Tue 21 Sep 09:00 PT works for Sarah and me. We prefer Helios-managed control plane for now (helps reduce our operational burden); can discuss longer-term options during the call.

I appreciate the detail in the upgrade/rollback plan — the USB fallback option is important for our change control.

Alex
